mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level increases the cost of capital for corporations, reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances despite FEDFUNDS level being above 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 2.5% indicates an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the labor market is strong (PAYEMS > 150,000) and inflation is elevated (CPIAUCSL > 300), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy aggressively, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 150000 and CPIAUCSL > 300.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (2017=100) indicates a weakening manufacturing sector, which typically precedes a recession and causes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100 during late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A positive quarterly change in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, which increases corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 change > 0.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% indicates weakening economic conditions, which increases the risk of recession and causes equity investors to sell, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects rising output in the manufacturing sector, which typically boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, producing positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO change > 0.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1400 thousand units and residential sales (RSAFS) decline below 680,000 million dollars, it indicates a contraction in the housing sector, reducing consumer spending and economic growth, which causes negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST < 1400 and RSAFS < 680000.
